items.t: The recent Starlink / Starshield incident in Ukraine has created a dangerous precedence for the US export industry, many haven't yet grasped. The sudden deacti
items.tx:
The recent Starlink / Starshield incident in Ukraine has created a dangerous precedence for the US export industry, many haven't yet grasped. The sudden deactivation respectively curtailing of those systems without warning not only cost precious lives, but also equipment worth millions.

Though the blame game between the White House (Trump) and SpaceX (Musk) is going on, ultimately it doesn't matter. It showed the world that the USA are not a reliable partner any more. Pointing at some obscure "violation of terms of services" without providing the exact passage are just increasing that notion that this was a political move.

The explanation that Starlink must not be used for "offensive" means is nonsense, too. Starlink has never been turned on over Russia, and using it in Ukraine is by definition defensive in nature. You can even argue that hitting Russian targets in Russia is defensive, since you don't have to wait for an attack to be conducted. Even the intention is enough to warrant action and to eliminate the threat at the source. But this is a different topic.

Furthermore, SpaceX has been fully aware that its Starlink terminals are being used by Ukrainian forces. Especially when considering that Ukraine only recently had to white-list their Starlink terminals for the Ukrainian military so that Russian forces, who have been abundantly using Starlink as well, were locked out. It has always been clear that those Starlink terminals are used for and by the Ukrainian military, and Ukraine has always been thankful for that.

Coming up with this bogus story, now, three weeks before midterms is therefore as transparent as it is shameless. It is obvious for everyone that this was just figleaf statement so that a political agenda can be pushed, an agenda which runs counter to the strategic nationalist interests of the USA, both political and economic.

And this is the real scandal. It is not new that the US had to lock out its technology or supplies to nations with which it had previously good and even cordial relation. Iran under the Shah, South-Vietnam and Cuba before Castro are just three to name it. But as you can see from them, it made perfectly sense back then. Those nations switched sides or disappeared altogether. 

Ukraine on the other hand didn't switch sides and even helped the US in the most recent and botched Iran war, despite being short on ammunition itself. The Ukrainian government accepted every possible compromise and offered an unconditional ceasefire from the start. Russia on the hand refused all of it and is demanding surrender. Yet, it gets this treatment? Unbelievable.

This will be noted by all clients around the globe who purchase US weapons and technology. If agreements are not honored and can unilaterally and even clandestinely be altered based on the whims of a few, who only follow their own motives or election lies, then the all concept reliability falls apart. 

Whether it is Starlink, the F-35, Tomahawk missiles or HIMARS. All those systems run on software and in many cases can only properly operate with recent updates. You don't even need have a kill switch. You can only refuse to update and many of those systems lose more than 90% of their effectiveness within a short period, making worthless.

This is why we see the blame game between Musk and Trump. I'm sure that people around those guys told them how absolutely shortsighted and stupid this step was. It will fall back on the entire US industry. Not even those two guys are worth that losses and backlash. A functional US Congress would immediately start subpoenas and hearings, asking questions in order to mitigate the damage, but here we are.

Trump and Musk have given the best reason why not to buy American. Customers - governmental and private alike - around the globe will take note of this and act accordingly, and I wouldn't be surprised if this won't be limited to US military products only. An absolutely senseless and avoidable own goal.

As an Iranian, we share a similar fate. A formerly wealthy and wonderful place, rich with oil and resources, and a bright, skilled population.

Ripped apart by a demonic regime willing to make the people suffer mass murder, torture, starvation and crippling poverty to keep their rule. Massive diasporas living in exile for decades, separated from our families.

Pure despair and hopelessness.

Few understand this suffering more than those of us who live it. Even fewer understand the feeling of watching these dictatorships finally fall.

And today, I see Venezuela's exiled opposition leader return to massive crowds, completely unopposed, zero communist thugs out to stop her. It's like a miracle happening.

It brings tears to my eyes watching oppressed people about to be liberated. It finally looks as if all of you in Venezuela will regain your freedom, your dignity, and your lost generations. Truly heartwarming and incredible.

It also makes me realise just how cursed Iran is to be trapped with an even more evil dictatorship. A regime who to this day refuses to give up even if it means the land turns to ashes and 90 million people lie killed in the ground. Venezuela's regime apparently now has the common sense to tell what time it is. Sadly, Iran is ruled by a whole other scale of barbarians.

May we one day soon witness our Shah return to a free Iran, just as you are lining the streets right now for your own leader across the ocean. May our countries prosper once more. May our diasporas finally reunite with our loved ones.

items.t: Volvo’s iconic “Epic Split” commercial starring Jean-Claude Van Damme remains one of the most remarkable advertising stunts ever captured on camera. Before fil
items.tx:
Volvo’s iconic “Epic Split” commercial starring Jean-Claude Van Damme remains one of the most remarkable advertising stunts ever captured on camera. Before filming, the truck drivers reportedly spent eight days practicing the intricate maneuver, perfecting the timing and positioning of two Volvo trucks reversing in formation. When Van Damme finally arrived, he positioned himself between their side mirrors and performed his legendary split as the vehicles gradually separated. Remarkably, the breathtaking sequence was reportedly completed in a single take, transforming days of meticulous preparation into an unforgettable cinematic moment.

What makes the stunt even more extraordinary is the incredible coordination required to execute it. Both trucks had to reverse at precisely controlled speeds while maintaining perfect alignment, leaving almost no room for error. At the same time, Van Damme relied on his exceptional flexibility, balance, and composure to hold the split as the distance between the vehicles increased. Contrary to the popular myth, his legs weren’t physically keeping the trucks apart. The illusion of effortless stability came from the drivers’ precision, extensive rehearsals, and carefully engineered execution.

The advertisement quickly became a viral phenomenon, combining an astonishing physical performance with brilliantly simple filmmaking. Van Damme’s peaceful expression, the slowly separating trucks, and the dramatic soundtrack created a moment that seemed almost too incredible to be real. Beyond showcasing his legendary athleticism, the stunt highlighted Volvo’s advanced steering technology and the extraordinary skill of its drivers. Eight days of preparation, one unforgettable take, and a commercial that secured its place in advertising history.

• Istanbul agreement, 2022

Ukraine needed to refuse NATO accession, reduce the army, Russia would withdraw from the Kyiv reg., possibly from the Kharkiv, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia regions. At that point the scale of destruction was still limited and the number of dead was far lower. In April 2022 Zelenskyy declined the deal.

Russian forces withdrew from part of the Kherson region. Zelenskyy traveled to meet Biden and, acc. to my sources, later confirmed by Mr. Blinken in the New York Times, persuaded the WH to continue the war. The precise terms of any proposed deal remain unknown, but sources indicate there was readiness to declare at least a ceasefire.

• Beginning of 2023

Through unofficial channels between the United States and Russia, an understanding took shape: Putin agreed to withdraw to the borders that existed before the full-scale invasion—freeing nearly everything conquered that year—in exchange for Ukraine’s refusal of NATO accession and recognition of Crimea as Russian. Zelenskyy and Yermak refused. Since then nearly a million people have been killed or wounded, several million have become refugees, parts of the Kharkiv, Sumy, and Dnipropetrovsk regions have been occupied, more of Zaporizhzhia has been taken, Kherson lies in ruins, the Chernihiv and Sumy regions face constant shelling, Kyiv itself has become almost a front-line city, the energy system has been destroyed, businesses cannot operate, exports have stalled, and the country is degrading.

• July 2024

Ukrainian MP confirms that 2023 peace plan, which was reported by @FT & accepted by Putin but rejected by Zelensky & Biden administration, envisioned:

"- Russia withdraws its troops from most of the four oblasts it had just declared “annexed.” 
- The new line of demarcation runs roughly along the line as of February 24, 2022: Crimea and the part of Donbas that Russia controlled before the full-scale invasion. 
- Ukraine recognizes Russian control over Crimea. - Ukraine grants Russia an unobstructed land corridor to Crimea. 
- The ceasefire regime is guaranteed by NATO countries that provide protection for Ukraine. 
- Russia begins negotiations with the US on its own security guarantees. 
-Moreover, Russia was ready to give up the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant as well. 
-And the 300 billion in frozen assets was to go toward rebuilding all of Ukraine, that is, together with the occupied territories. 
-As for Crimea: we were not required to recognize it as Russian, only to recognize Russia’s control over it. In other words, we acknowledge that right now it is under Russian control (which is how it is). We were also required to adopt a law banning the return of Crimea by military means. 
-The land corridor to Crimea, a highway and a railway, was to be built at Russia’s expense. The hardest question was how to guard it. That is why the Russians were ready to give up Melitopol, but not Tokmak: they feared we would cut the corridor with artillery. 
-Zelensky rejected this proposal at the time."

In recent months, the Americans, French, Germans, and Israelis - our so-called “allies” - have either cast doubt on our sovereignty over the Falkland Islands or moved towards supplying weapons to Argentina, a country that continues to claim British territory as its own.

President Trump has openly discussed reviewing America's position on the Falklands. French and German defence firms have offered Argentina new submarines, while Israel has already signed an agreement to supply its armed forces with weapons.

What is our government doing in response?

Nothing.

We may not be the global superpower we once were, but we still have tremendous leverage over all of these countries and we should not be afraid of using it.

And I don’t mean sending strongly-worded letters or summoning ambassadors. 

The government has already negotiated surrender deals over Chagos and Gibraltar. If we continue to allow our territorial integrity to be questioned without consequence, we will lose all of our overseas territories and be left even more globally irrelevant than we already are.

BREAKING: Iran is now threatening to strike Israel's Sorek, Hadera, Ashdod and Ashkelon desalination plants; Haifa oil refineries; the Orot Rabin and Eshkol power plants; Ashdod oil refineries and fuel storage; the Dimona nuclear research center; and critical bridges and highway interchanges if Israel and the U.S. launch another attack on Iran, according to head of Iran's parliamentary National Security Commission.

Desalination facilities supply around 80% of Israel's municipal drinking water. Orot Rabin (2,590 MW) and Eshkol (912 MW) anchor the national grid. The Haifa refinery processes roughly 197,000 barrels per day, while Ashdod adds 110,000 bpd. Highway 6, the country's main artery, carries 260,000 vehicles daily. And Dimona sits just 13 kilometers from the city. Tehran is threatening to paralyze Israel's water, power, fuel, and mobilization routes in one blow.
